name: AI Swarm Problem Solver
tag: A team of AI agents takes a business problem apart, tests causes against your data and ranks the fixes.

scenarios.title: Fix late warehouse shipments
scenarios.ask: Our warehouse ships {orders} orders a week and {=late}% go out late. Why, and what should we fix first?
steps: Data agent
Read {orders} sample orders. Late orders cluster on Mondays and on multi-item picks.
Hypothesis agent
Tested 5 explanations. Weekend backlog and pick-path length explain 78% of delays.
Critic agent
Rejected 'carrier delays': on-time rate is the same across carriers.
Cost agent
A Saturday half-shift for {staff} people costs about ${=staff * 4 * 22} a week at a sample $22 an hour.
Planner
Ranked fixes by impact and effort.

result.title: Top fix
rows: About {=round(orders * late / 100 * (1 - max(0.35, 0.6 - staff * 0.03)))} a week

followups: How sure are you about the cause?
The two causes explain 78% of delays in this sample. The swarm shows the data behind each, and the Critic agent lists what it could not rule out.
The Critic agent checked: on-time pickup is the same across carriers, so switching would add cost without fixing the backlog.
Moving the top 50 SKUs near packing shortens pick paths. Together with the shift, the sample model puts the late rate near {=round(late * max(0.25, 0.5 - staff * 0.03), 1)}%.

scenarios.title: Find why customers are leaving
scenarios.ask: We have {customers} customers and monthly churn rose to {=churn}%. What is driving it?
steps: Data agent
Joined account, billing and support data for {customers} customers.
Hypothesis agent
Tested 6 explanations. Customers who never set up the second feature leave 3 times as often.
Critic agent
Rejected 'the price rise': churn rose the same for customers who were not affected by it.
Planner
Ranked fixes: an onboarding nudge for the second feature first, a check-in call for large accounts second.

result.title: Top fix
rows: Medium: test on half of new accounts first

followups: Splitting new accounts lets you see if the nudge itself lowers churn, instead of a change that happened at the same time.
Can the swarm read support tickets?
Yes. It groups tickets by topic and checks whether any topic shows up more often before a customer leaves.

scenarios.title: Explain a regional sales drop
scenarios.ask: Sales in one of our {regions} regions fell {=drop}% this quarter. Find out why.
steps: Data agent
Compared deals, pipeline and pricing across all {regions} regions.
Hypothesis agent
Tested 4 explanations. New pipeline fell after {=max(1, round(reps * 0.25))} rep(s) left in month one.
Critic agent
Rejected 'a competitor price cut': win rates against that competitor did not change.
Planner
Suggested moving accounts from departed reps within a week and a short lead-generation push.

result.title: Findings
rows: Two quarters if accounts are reassigned now

followups: What else could be going on?
The Critic agent lists what it could not test, such as local economic changes. You can add that data and rerun.
Does it replace a sales review?
No. It gives the review a ranked list of causes and evidence so the meeting can focus on decisions.
